explanations: submit() frees the worker slot (active-- and startNext()) only when a task succeeds. When a task rejects, the rejection goes straight to the caller, but active stays incremented and the next queued task is never started. Each failed encode permanently takes one slot, so after `size` failures the pool thinks it is full forever, and everything queued behind it waits even though nothing runs. The fix releases the slot and starts the next task in a finally, so a slot comes back however the task ends.
